::: {#exm-konigsberg}
#### The bridges of K&ouml;nigsberg

The city of K&ouml;nigsberg was built on four pieces of land, divided by a river,
with seven bridges between them [@wikipedia_seven_bridges_of_konigsberg].
Name the pieces of land $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$, where $A$ is an island.
Two bridges joined $A$ and $B$,
two joined $A$ and $C$,
and one bridge joined each of the pairs $\set{A, D}$, $\set{B, D}$ and $\set{C, D}$.

@fig-konigsberg draws the graph (@def-graph-vertices-edges) with a vertex for each piece of land and an edge for each bridge.
It has two pairs of parallel edges (@def-parallel-edges), and no loops (@def-graph-loop).

::: {#fig-konigsberg}

![](../images/graphs-konigsberg.png){fig-alt="Four points A, B, C and D. A is in the middle of a column, with B above and C below. Two curved lines join A and B, two curved lines join A and C, and single lines join A to D, B to D and C to D, where D is to the right." width="35%"}

The bridges of K&ouml;nigsberg as a graph: a vertex for each piece of land, and an edge for each bridge.

:::
